issues.description: Preview contract is documented by example only; no written spec for the abstract type
issues.detail: The docs introduce a family of subtypes (JsonPreview, TablePreview, PlotlyPreview, MermaidPreview, ImagePreview, TextPreview, CustomPreview) but never state the supertype contract: required fields, allowed content types per subtype, what to_dict() guarantees, or what preview() may raise. Without a stated contract, callers and future subtypes cannot honor LSP. Add a Preview ADT section before the per-type sections.

issues.description: TablePreview precondition is stronger than peers, hidden in a Note
issues.detail: TablePreview requires content as list[dict] while JsonPreview/TextPreview/MermaidPreview accept their natural types. That is a stronger precondition on one subtype and should be surfaced as part of the contract, not a parenthetical. Document the per-subtype content schema explicitly so substitution expectations are visible and a DataFrame-passing caller fails predictably.

issues.description: meta is overloaded: general metadata and renderer config share one channel
issues.detail: Docs explicitly state meta serves two purposes: contextual metadata and rendering configuration (Mermaid layout, code language). This conflates two distinct contracts through one untyped dict, leaking renderer implementation concerns into the abstraction. Recommend separating: meta for opaque context, and a typed render_config (or per-subtype field like language) for renderer hints. At minimum, document the reserved keys.

issues.description: CustomPreview renderer_key contract is unstated; abstraction leaks frontend coupling
issues.detail: CustomPreview is described as identifying which frontend component renders it, which makes the backend node abstraction depend on a Kedro-Viz-side registry that is nowhere specified. Define: who owns the renderer_key namespace, what happens when the key is unknown, and whether unknown keys are an error or a no-op. Otherwise this is a LEAKY-ABSTRACTION across the kedro/kedro-viz boundary.

issues.description: preview_fn signature and error semantics are unspecified
issues.detail: Docs say preview functions don't have access to node inputs or outputs and suggest closures, but never state the required signature (zero-arg?), whether async is allowed, what node.preview() returns if preview_fn is absent, or how exceptions propagate. Best-practice item 5 says wrap in try/except if needed without defining what kedro does on failure. State preconditions and postconditions of preview_fn and node.preview().

issues.description: Experimental warning lacks a stability contract for the preview type hierarchy
issues.detail: The experimental banner warns the feature may change but gives callers no contract for how subtypes may evolve: can new required fields be added to existing previews, can renderer_key behavior change, will to_dict() shape stay stable across minor releases. A short stability note (what is frozen, what is not) would let users adopt this without coupling to unspecified internals.

review.summary: The PR documents a new node-preview feature built around a family of typed Preview subtypes, but the docs describe behavior by example rather than stating the abstract contract. The supertype's promised shape, the per-subtype content preconditions, and the semantics of node.preview() and preview_fn are not written down, which makes substitution and future extension fragile. meta is overloaded as both opaque metadata and renderer configuration, and CustomPreview's renderer_key leaks a Kedro-Viz frontend dependency through the kedro node API without specifying ownership or failure modes. Recommend adding an explicit Preview ADT section (preconditions, postconditions, invariants, to_dict shape), separating render config from meta, and pinning the preview_fn signature and error contract before this leaves experimental.
